body: How cool is that! I didn't know that the current context is written to `~/.kube/config`. Just tested this on my machine as well (Mac).
😎 . I'm no performance expert but it's probably better to declare this outside of the function?
Not saying you have to do that in this PR but you can also replace this mutable `ns` + break with a filter and a fold

Nice test setup. I would suggest to add one more test with multiple contexts. Let me lend you one similar to mine 😉 
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789:cluster/eks-cluster-eu-west-1-dev
    user: arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789:cluster/eks-cluster-eu-west-1-dev
  name: DEV
- context:
    cluster: arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789:cluster/eks-cluster-eu-west-1-prod
    user: arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789:cluster/eks-cluster-eu-west-1-prod
  name: PROD
current-context: DEV

```
As I'm writing this, I notice that namespace detection would not work with my setup. I don't have one namespace per context but use multiple dev namespaces within the dev context. Not sure if it's best practice to include the namespace in the context? I have to say I like not having to switch so often and if I do it's to get to PROD. But yeah I see that in this case it's impossible to show the namespace, so nvm.

Would still add the test 🙃
And maybe we could note in the documentation that namespace detection only works if namespaces are bound to contexts
I agree with this. `let mut ns` and a `for` loop doesn't feel very rusty.
It's a `const`, so it won't have a performance impact, but it may be neater to declare it at the top of the file

can't get it to compile and have to go but something like this?
```
    let ns: Option<&str> = conf["contexts"].as_vec().and_then(|contexts| {
        contexts
            .iter()
            .filter(|ctx| ctx["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("") == current_ctx)
            .map(|ctx| ctx["context"]["namespace"].as_str().unwrap_or(""))
            .collect()
            .get(0)
    });
```

Hmm, Is this simpler?

```
    let ns = conf["contexts"]
        .as_vec()
        .and_then(|contexts| {
            contexts
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|ctx| Some((ctx, ctx["name"].as_str()?)))
                .find(|(_, name)| *name == current_ctx)
                .and_then(|(ctx, _)| ctx["context"]["namespace"].as_str())
        })
        .unwrap_or("");
```
